t: Section 788(b)(4) of the Public Health Service Act shall not apply to any grant made under section 788(b) of that Act from funds appropriated under the provision headed “Health resources” in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare Appropriations Act, 1979.

fable.w: This provision only exempts certain grants funded by a specific appropriation from a statutory requirement. The tempting reading is that grant-related language implies outside involvement, but grants are not participation under the definition. The section has no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: Section 788(b)(4) of the Public Health Service Act shall not apply to any grant made under section 788(b) of that Act

opus.w: This section only says that a grant condition in the Public Health Service Act does not apply to certain grants paid for with 1979 appropriations. It does not create any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The mention of grants is not participation: grant matters are expressly excluded, and the waived provision's content is not shown here.
opus.s: Section 788(b)(4) of the Public Health Service Act shall not apply to any grant made under section 788(b) of that Act

qwen_chat.w: This section exempts a specific grant program from a statutory requirement. It does not create a mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government, comment on decisions, or participate in advisory bodies. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants from the scope of participation, and this text merely modifies the administrative rules governing those grants without introducing external participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 788(b)(4) of the Public Health Service Act shall not apply to any grant made under section 788(b) of that Act from funds appropriated under the provision headed “Health resources” in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare Appropriations Act, 1979.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because grants are mentioned, and grants often involve applications or oversight, this could imply participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. Furthermore, this section merely exempts a specific grant program from a reporting or procedural requirement (Section 788(b)(4)); it does not establish a new process for outside parties to consult with the government, nor does it grant rights to sue or comment. It is a limitation on administrative procedure, not a mechanism for public participation.
